content.text: No minimum purchase or take-or-pay obligation exists anywhere in the agreement. Submitting a compliant finding.

input.quote: (a) Ono shall have the right (but not the obligation) to Manufacture and/or package, or engage a Subcontractor to Manufacture, Ono's requirements of particular Materials
input.rationale: The rule is met at the preferred position: nothing in the Agreement imposes a minimum purchase commitment, take-or-pay, shortfall penalty or volume cap on Ono. Article IX is structured entirely as a supply obligation running in our favour — Array "shall supply, or secure supply of, Ono's requirements" (9.1(a), 9.4(b)(i) "Ono's reasonable requirements"), and 9.4(a) expressly gives Ono "the right (but not the obligation)" to manufacture or dual-source through its own Subcontractor, so we are not locked into buying from Array at all. Forecasting/ordering mechanics are deferred to future clinical and commercial supply agreements (9.3(a), 9.4(b)(i)) and contain no committed volumes here; any minimum-order or firm-forecast terms should be resisted when those agreements are negotiated. Financial terms are consumption- and success-based: royalties are payable on actual Net Sales (6.3) and milestones on achievement of events, with no minimum annual royalty or maintenance fee. Ono also holds an exit — termination without cause on notice (13.2) plus Safety/Efficacy termination (13.5). Noted but not flagged: the ¥3.5bn upfront licence fee is non-refundable and non-creditable (6.1), but that is an entry fee for the licence rather than a volume commitment, and Article VIII diligence/exclusivity obligations are effort-based ("Diligent Efforts"), not volume-based. No redline required.
